name: Developer authored the fix → measure the task in-container + count the attempt
description:
The measure station (design SB4, group 7B). When a DEVELOPER loop (Amelia) terminates successfully — she authored the fix and apply_patch applied it cleanly to the run's checkout — the harness measures the REAL, in-container outcome: it forces measure_task, which Execs the task's IMMUTABLE test command in the run's WARM sandbox container (the one provision_sandbox stood up over the same checkout apply_patch wrote) and stamps the harness-derived measurement.result (G3 — the model supplies no command and no outcome). This is the make-or-break both predecessors faked: the pass/fail is of the artifact BUILT COLD in the operator-declared image, not a host process nor a model claim.

TRIGGER = the developer LOOP TERMINAL, not an apply_patch fact. It fires on agent.loop.role=developer AND agent.loop.outcome=success. agent.loop.role is stamped at SPAWN (WriteSpawnIdentity, present throughout the loop's life); agent.loop.outcome is stamped at completion by WriteLoopCompletion — so the terminal transition brings outcome to "success" with role already present, a robust real trigger. Gating on outcome=success is load-bearing: a FAILED apply also stamps an outcome, and measuring an unapplied checkout would be theater. Each retry mints a FRESH developer loop, so this rule re-fires per attempt FOR FREE (a fresh loop carries no dev.measured marker).

ATTEMPT COUNTER: on_enter appends task.attempt.0 on the RUN entity (subject-override $entity.triple.agent.run.entity_id — the developer loop carries the run anchor) with object=$entity.instance (the developer loop instance). It is an APPENDED multi-triple counter, not an upsert: a distinct object per attempt (the loop instance) so identical attempts do not collapse under graph-ingest set-dedup — the budget/retry gate (group 7D) counts task.attempt.0's cardinality against task.spec.0.budget. Appended at the loop terminal (not at dispatch) because a run-fired retry cannot mint a distinct object, but the loop instance can — so it counts every attempt including retries. (Single task at M0 → the literal index 0; multi-task needs per-index rule copies, a field cannot template <i>.)

MEASURE LOOP: run_scope=inherit reads the developer loop's bare agent.run and binds the spawned measure loop's RunID to the same run, so measure_task resolves THIS run's warm sandbox + task.spec from its tool-call metadata. ROLE = coordinator (NOT developer) — deliberately: a developer-role measure loop would itself reach outcome=success and RE-TRIGGER this very rule (an unbounded measure→measure loop). A coordinator loop calling a harness tool is the established pattern (provision_sandbox, project_tasks): tool_choice=function forces measure_task and tools stays nil (global discovery), the loop calls it and StopLoops (measure_task StopLoops on its success return), writing measurement.result (not coordinator.decision.*), so it triggers no coordinator decision rule and no dispatch. It is a measuring turn, not a routing or authoring turn.

SELF-EXTINGUISHING ONE-SHOT (restart-safe): on_enter FIRST stamps the fired-once marker dev.measured=$entity.instance on the DEVELOPER loop (the firing entity), and the dev.measured length_eq 0 guard makes the trigger flip false the moment it fires. This is the house restart-safety pattern (semteams agent-run/02, dev-from-task/02/03/04): publish_agent is NOT idempotent (each fire mints a fresh measure loop; the framework does not dedup), and role+outcome stay stamped, so WITHOUT this marker a graph replay with RULE_STATE lost (ENTITY_STATES surviving — asymmetric bucket loss) would re-spawn a DUPLICATE measure loop. The marker (a durable ENTITY_STATES triple on the loop) closes that independent of RULE_STATE. Marker stamped BEFORE the publish so a publish failure leaves the run stuck-toward-human rather than duplicated. LOOP-scoped (like dev.dispatched) because this rule fires on the developer loop. The attempt append is idempotent per loop (a re-fire of the SAME loop appends the same object → set-dedup collapses it), so it is safe alongside the marker.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.coordinator
on_enter.prompt: SEMDEV — the developer authored the fix and the harness applied it to this run's checkout. Now measure the developed task in the sandbox: call measure_task with task_index 0. The harness runs the task's frozen test command IN the run's warm container (built cold from the operator-declared image) and records the real exit code — you supply no command and claim no outcome. Calling measure_task completes your turn.

metadata.station: measure_task — run the frozen test command in the warm sandbox on the developer-loop terminal (SB4, 7B)
metadata.trigger_rationale: fires on the developer loop's SUCCESSFUL terminal (agent.loop.role=developer, stamped at spawn; agent.loop.outcome=success, stamped at completion by WriteLoopCompletion). outcome=success excludes a failed apply (never measure an unapplied checkout). A fresh developer loop per retry re-fires this for free.
metadata.role_rationale: coordinator, NOT developer — a developer-role measure loop would re-satisfy this rule's own trigger (outcome=success) and loop unboundedly. A coordinator loop forced to a harness tool is the provision/project pattern; measure_task stamps measurement.result (not coordinator.decision.*) so it triggers no decision rule and StopLoops on success.
metadata.attempt_counter: on_enter appends task.attempt.0 on the run (subject-override the loop's agent.run.entity_id; object=$entity.instance, the developer loop instance). APPEND, not upsert: a rule add_triple goes through graph-ingest's UNCONDITIONAL append (no dedup/property-replace), so the group-7D budget gate MUST count DISTINCT OBJECTS of task.attempt.0 (the loop instance) against task.spec.0.budget — never raw triple cardinality. Distinct-object counting is robust to the at-least-once mutation (a lost ack retries and double-appends the SAME object) and still counts every real attempt. Appended at the loop terminal (not dispatch) because only the loop instance is a distinct per-attempt object a run-fired retry could not mint.
metadata.restart_safe: SELF-EXTINGUISHING via the LOOP-scoped dev.measured marker + length_eq 0 guard (house pattern). publish_agent is not idempotent, so the one-shot is intrinsic (not reliant on RULE_STATE); measure_task's StopLoop keeps the measure loop one turn. Marker stamped BEFORE the publish so a publish failure stalls-toward-human rather than duplicating. In the normal path the marker bounds task.attempt.0 to one append per developer loop; the append is NOT idempotent at the graph layer (add_triple appends unconditionally, and the mutation is at-least-once), which is why the 7D gate counts distinct objects rather than raw cardinality (see attempt_counter).
metadata.g3: measure_task takes only task_index — the command is read from the immutable task.spec and the outcome is derived from the real in-container exit code. The model may only TRIGGER the measurement, never supply the command or the result.
metadata.token_handshake_deferred: the per-attempt token handshake (measure stamps measurement.result.<i>.attempt, check_floors echoes it, the gate consumes it) lands with the floors-gate in group 7C/7D — the token has no consumer until the gate exists. This rule sets up the counter (task.attempt.<i>) the gate reads; the correlation token is 7C's addition.
metadata.deferred_tool_scoping: tools omitted = global discovery. tool_choice=function:measure_task structurally constrains the call, so this is largely closed; the residual is populating bootstrap allowed_tools + a scoped tools list before the first real-LLM token (the coordinated MEDIUM-3 change). Inert under the mock (positional cursor).
